Int align

resharper_int_align_declaration_names #

Column-align declaration names. Not read by the C# formatter, on two measurements rather than one. (1) true one key away from the export returns a probe of adjacent fields, locals, assignments and enum members byte-identical. (2) The stronger question — "is that a fact about the probe, or about the key?" — asked with resharper_int_align = true supplied as well, so every resharper_csharp_int_align_* key is on and a run exists at every one of those shapes: turning this key off on top of that changes nothing. The column it claims to govern is produced by resharper_csharp_int_align_fields and …_variables and is indifferent to this spelling.

Default known fromthe Rider export, which is Rider's default for most keys and the author's choice for the rest, with nothing distinguishing the two

resharper_int_align_enum_initializers #

Column-align enum member initializers. Not read by the C# formatter, on two measurements. (1) true one key away from the export returns two probe enums whose member names differ in width byte-identical. (2) With resharper_int_align = true supplied — which does pad both enums' = into a column — turning this key off on top of that changes nothing. resharper_csharp_int_align_fields is what aligns an enum's initializers; this spelling is the C++ and VB formatters'.

resharper_int_align_eq #

Column-align = signs. Named by docs/plan/05 § "Alignment" and dropped by the M0 importer. Not read by the C# formatter, on two measurements. (1) true one key away from the export returns a probe of adjacent fields, locals and assignments byte-identical. (2) With resharper_int_align = true supplied — which does pad every one of those = into a column — turning this key off on top of that changes nothing. The = column is resharper_csharp_int_align_{fields,variables,assignments}'; this spelling is the C++ and VB formatters'.
